---
title: "Lordicon Extension for Quarto"
resources:
  - gift_raw.json
---

This extension lets you embed animated [Lordicon](https://lordicon.com) icons in your Quarto HTML documents (including Reveal.js slides). Icons can be pulled from the official CDN or loaded from local `.json` files, and customized on the fly without editing the source files.

## Showcase

{{< li laqlvddb trigger=loop delay=1000 >}}  {{< li egmlnyku trigger=loop delay=2000 >}} {{< li bmlkvhui trigger=loop delay=3000 >}} {{< li aqrzgjfy trigger=loop delay=4000 >}}

## Source

The `{{{< li >}}}` shortcode downloads an icon from the Lordicon CDN and renders it by its **code** — the eight-character identifier in `https://cdn.lordicon.com/CODE.json`. Lordicon used to hand these out under Export → Embed HTML; the redesigned export UI no longer offers that, so existing codes still resolve but new icons are easier to use via `{{{< lif >}}}`.

The `{{{< lif >}}}` shortcode renders an icon from a local `.json` **file** instead. Download one by opening an icon on [lordicon.com](https://lordicon.com/icons), clicking **Edit and download**, then in the right-hand panel opening the format menu and clicking the options icon next to **Lottie**.

That options icon offers two Lottie flavors, and which one you want depends on where you plan to customize the icon:

- **Minified** (the default) bakes the editor's colors and stroke into the shapes and keeps only the animation you picked. Much smaller file, and the right choice when the icon already looks the way you want.
- **Raw** keeps every animation along with the control layer that `colors`, `stroke`, and `state` write into. Choose this to customize per use from the shortcode.

::: {.callout-note}
The two approaches don't combine: `colors`, `stroke`, and `state` have no effect on a minified file, since those values were baked in at export. Either re-export as Raw or set them in the editor and leave the arguments off. The extension prints a warning when it sees that combination.
:::

| Shortcode                       | Rendered                    |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| `{{{< li ibydboev >}}}`         | {{< li ibydboev >}}         |
| `{{{< lif gift_raw.json >}}}`   | {{< lif gift_raw.json >}}   |

## Colors

`colors` recolors an icon. Outline icons usually have just a primary and secondary color, while flat and lineal icons can have many more. Give each color in `rank:color` form (ranks are `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, …) and separate multiple colors with commas. Colors accept HTML color names or hex codes.

| Shortcode                            | Icon                             |
|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `{{{< li rehjpyyh >}}}`              | {{< li rehjpyyh >}}              |
| `{{{< li rehjpyyh colors=primary:gold >}}}`   | {{< li rehjpyyh colors=primary:gold >}}   |
| `{{{< li rehjpyyh colors=secondary:gold >}}}`   | {{< li rehjpyyh colors=secondary:gold >}}   |
| `{{{< li rehjpyyh colors=primary:gray,secondary:orange >}}}`   | {{< li rehjpyyh colors=primary:gray,secondary:orange >}}   |
| `{{{< li rehjpyyh colors=primary:#4030e8,secondary:#ee66aa >}}}`   | {{< li rehjpyyh colors=primary:#4030e8,secondary:#ee66aa >}}   |

## Stroke

`stroke` sets how thick the lines of a (supported) icon are: `light`, `regular`, or `bold`.

| Shortcode                             | Icon                               |
|---------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `{{{< li rehjpyyh stroke=light >}}}`     | {{< li rehjpyyh stroke=light >}}      |
| `{{{< li rehjpyyh stroke=regular >}}}`     | {{< li rehjpyyh stroke=regular >}}      |
| `{{{< li rehjpyyh stroke=bold >}}}`     | {{< li rehjpyyh stroke=bold >}}      |

## Accessibility

Icons are decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`). When an icon carries meaning, pass a `label` and it is exposed to screen readers with `role="img"` and that name.

ARIA attributes you pass yourself take precedence. Passing a non-empty `aria-hidden`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or `role` stops the extension from adding `aria-hidden="true"`. With `label`, your own `role` or `aria-label` replaces the one that `label` adds. These four names count in any letter case, so `Role` or `ARIA-LABEL` works the same way. When you set `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` directly, also pass `role="img"` so screen readers announce the icon.

If an icon gets an image role (`img`, `image`, or `graphics-symbol`) but no name, the render warns. A screen reader then cannot say what the icon shows. The render reads the first word of `role` that names a non-abstract role in the ARIA specs, which is the rule that WAI-ARIA gives browsers. These specs are WAI-ARIA 1.2, DPUB-ARIA 1.1, and Graphics-ARIA 1.0, plus `image`. So `role="bogus img"` warns, and `role="presentation img"` does not. A name comes from `label`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or `title`. If you also pass `aria-hidden="true"`, `hidden`, or `inert`, the render does not warn.

| Shortcode                             | Icon                               |
|---------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `{{{< li ibydboev >}}}` *(decorative)* | {{< li ibydboev >}}      |
| `{{{< li ibydboev label="Money bag" >}}}` | {{< li ibydboev label="Money bag" >}}      |
| `{{{< li ibydboev role="img" aria-label="Money bag" >}}}` | {{< li ibydboev role="img" aria-label="Money bag" >}}      |
